Can AI Really Save You Money? 7 Tools to Try and Compare

Can AI really help you spend less? Explore seven tools for writing, design, research, video editing, and automation, and learn how to compare their costs against the value they provide.

By LokkeeVerse · 4 min read

Can AI Really Save You Money? 7 Tools to Try and Compare

AI tools promise to save time, reduce costs, and help you do more with less. But can they actually save you money?

The answer depends on how you use them. A free AI assistant might help you write content without hiring a writer for every small task, while an AI design tool could reduce the time you spend creating social media graphics.

Here are seven AI tools worth comparing before spending money on subscriptions or services.

1. ChatGPT — Save Time on Writing

Website: https://chatgpt.com/

ChatGPT can help you draft emails, brainstorm business ideas, write product descriptions, and outline articles.

Instead of starting every piece of content from scratch, you can use it to create a first draft and refine it yourself.

Potential savings: Less time spent on routine writing and brainstorming.

2. Canva — Reduce Basic Design Costs

Website: https://www.canva.com/

Canva offers templates and design tools that help you create social media posts, flyers, presentations, and marketing graphics.

For a small business, it can reduce the need to hire a designer for every simple promotional image.

Potential savings: Lower costs for routine graphics and promotional materials.

3. CapCut — Edit Videos Without Expensive Software

Website: https://www.capcut.com/

CapCut offers video-editing features, captions, effects, and selected AI tools that can help simplify content production.

Creators can use it to produce short videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts without immediately paying for professional editing software.

Potential savings: Reduced basic editing expenses and faster video production.

4. Perplexity — Speed Up Research

Website: https://www.perplexity.ai/

Perplexity helps you research topics by providing answers with links to sources.

It can be useful when comparing products, investigating competitors, or gathering background information before making a business decision.

Potential savings: Less time spent searching across multiple websites.

Always verify important claims before making financial or business decisions.

5. Grammarly — Improve Your Writing

Website: https://www.grammarly.com/

Grammarly helps identify grammar, spelling, and clarity issues in your writing.

It can be useful for polishing emails, proposals, website content, and customer communications before sending them.

Potential savings: Less time spent correcting routine writing errors.

6. Zapier — Automate Repetitive Work

Website: https://zapier.com/

Zapier connects supported apps so that repetitive tasks can happen automatically.

For example, you could create a workflow that saves new customer enquiries to a spreadsheet and sends a notification when a new lead arrives.

Potential savings: Less manual administration and fewer repetitive actions.

Check the free plan's limits before building a workflow you depend on.

7. Google Gemini — Get Everyday AI Assistance

Website: https://gemini.google.com/

Gemini can help with brainstorming, summarizing information, explaining concepts, and drafting content.

It may be a useful alternative if you need an AI assistant for everyday tasks but don't want another paid subscription.

Potential savings: Fewer paid AI subscriptions for tasks its free access can handle.

How to Tell Whether AI Is Actually Saving You Money

Using an AI tool doesn't automatically mean you're spending less. You should compare the total cost with the time and money saved.

Try this simple approach:

  • Choose one task that regularly costs you money or time.
  • Record how much you currently spend completing it.
  • Test an AI tool on the same task.
  • Include subscription fees, editing time, and any additional costs.
  • Compare the quality of the results before deciding whether to keep using it.

For example, if a tool costs ₦10,000 per month but saves you only ₦3,000 worth of work, it may not be worthwhile. If it consistently saves more than it costs without reducing quality, it could be a sensible investment.

Final Verdict

AI can help reduce expenses, but the best results come from choosing tools that solve real problems.

Start with free plans, compare the results, and pay only when a tool provides enough value to justify its cost. Remember that free plans may have usage limits, and some tasks still require professional expertise.

The goal isn't to use as many AI tools as possible. It's to spend less where you can while maintaining the quality of your work.
